title: devbin macos store-creds puts each Apple notary credential, the app-specific password among them, in security(1)'s argv
body:
## What

`bin/devbin macos store-creds` (Utilz's handler, `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`, `cmd_store_creds`) reads the three Apple notary credentials at the terminal, then stores each with `security add-generic-password ... -w "$v"`. The value goes on security(1)'s command line, so for the life of each call any local process can read it with `ps` or `sysctl kern.procargs2`. Among those values is APPLE_APP_PASSWORD, the app-specific password that notarises as hv's Apple account.

devbin's built-in `macos store-creds` (`bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/macos`) ends each `security` call with a bare `-w`, so security(1) prompts for the value itself and it never reaches an argv.

## Severity and exposure

Low. The window is the moment of each `security` call. The command runs only by hand in hv's own terminal on hv's single-user Mac, and rarely (once per credential change). A reader would need a process already running as a local user at that moment. Not a showstopper.

## Deferred

hv's standing rule, 28 Oct 2026, through molt-vc: "Any security issues need to be properly filed. We're just not fixing them now unless they're showstopper P0s." Deferred, not in 2.14.6. Not started.

The fix comes either way:
- With issue 0118, when Utilz's handler converges on devbin's built-in macos, whose store-creds already prompts through security(1).
- Earlier only if hv asks: pass a bare `-w` as the built-in does, and drop the handler's own reads of the values.

## Source

Found in ic's read-only comparison of the two handlers (27 Oct, `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-ic/devbin-macos-comparison.md`, "store-creds"), checked against the code by utilz-vc on 28 Oct: `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`, the `security add-generic-password` line in `cmd_store_creds`.

## Closed

Gone with Utilz's handler in issue 0118, landed at 511f47dc and checked by vc by its change (29 Oct). The built-in store-creds ends each security(1) call with a bare -w, so the value is typed at security's own prompt and never reaches an argv.
